title: Add prefetch-effectiveness metrics, token-position heatmap, and kernel-warmup traces
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: we continue to see intermittent latency spikes driven by cold kernel invocations and inefficient prefetch behavior for long prefixes. This PR introduces a set of observability artifacts to surface prefetch effectiveness (hit/miss/age distribution), a token-position cost/latency heatmap, and lightweight kernel-warmup traces so SRE and runtime teams can correlate cold starts with token-level cost.

What this PR adds (summary): 1) metric: runtime.prefetch.hit_ratio and runtime.prefetch.age_bucketed (tiled histogram) by model+pool, exposed via metrics pipeline; 2) metric: token.position.heatmap (downsampled 2D histogram keyed by model, route, and sequence-length-bin); 3) tracing: kernel.warmup.span with attributes (model, device_type, kernel_id, warmup_phase, kv_prefetched) and short-span sampling at 1% with deterministic reservoir for correlation; 4) dashboard: "Prefetch & Warmup" Grafana dashboard with three panels (prefetch hit-ratio over time, token-position heatmap, recent kernel-warmup traces linked to trace IDs); 5) alert: prefetch-miss-rate-high (SLO-aware reframe) that auto-suppresses during known release windows and triggers a debug runbook.

Implementation notes: - Metrics are emitted from runtime/prefetch_manager and aggregated in observability/metrics/exporter with a compact histogram encoding to keep cardinality low. - Token-position heatmap is calculated in the invocation summarizer: we sample the first 256 positions and bucket by quartiles of sequence length. The heatmap uses a tiled downsampled store so dashboards don't fetch raw high-cardinality series. - Kernel warmup spans are added to the kernel scheduler hot path; spans are created only when (a) a kernel requires binary reinitialization or (b) prefetch miss triggers a fallback path. Warmup spans are intentionally short and use a special trace tag to avoid inflating normal trace retention. - Dashboard JSON lives in observability/dashboards/prefetch-warmup.json and includes drilldowns to the trace explorer and cost explorer panels.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests: metrics encoders and histogram bucketers (runtime/prefetch_manager/*_test.go). - Integration: end-to-end run in the perf-lab using a synthetic workload that simulates long prefix usage (script: perf-lab/synthetic/prefetch-smoke.sh). - Observability QA: deployed dashboard to staging and verified correlations between forced kernel reloads and heatmap spikes. - Performance: microbench shows ~0.6% p99 latency delta at very high QPS when warmup spans are enabled; span sampling and downsampling mitigations keep steady-state overhead <0.2%.

Rollout plan: feature flagged behind observability.prefetch_warmup_metrics. Initial rollout to staging (complete), then canary to 5% of edge pools for 48 hours, then 25% for 24 hours, then global. Alert created in staging and set to notify the runtime-oncall channel in canary.

Docs and runbook: added runtime/docs/prefetch-metrics.md with metric definitions, alerting thresholds, and a short runbook for on-call. The runbook outlines steps to confirm whether a spike is caused by model variant changes, kernel kernel-cache eviction, or network-mounted model manifests.

Related work: complements ENG-2086 (kv-cache-profiler) and ENG-2310 (token-heatmap-exploration). Not a replacement for model cost attribution work but provides high-fidelity signals useful for root cause.

Notes: kept cardinality low by scoping metrics at model+pool and bucketing sequence lengths; token-position heatmap is intentionally approximate to avoid explosion of series.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can we ensure prefetch metrics are namespaced to model+pool only? high cardinality was our previous pain.
Asha Patel: Yes — metrics are emitted with model and pool tags only; variant and tenant are not present. Added explicit tests to prove card remains bounded.
Linus Chen: The kernel warmup span looks useful, but confirm it doesn't OOM the trace backend when we enable at scale.
Asha Patel: Warmup spans are sampled at 1% and tagged with a deterministic reservoir id; also we exclude warmup spans from high-retention index. Added docs/tracing note.
Marta Kovacs: Alert threshold tuning feels aggressive; suggest using SLO-relative thresholds and a mute window for deployments.
Asha Patel: Updated alert to be SLO-aware and added an auto-suppress rule during release windows in the alert yaml.
release_notes: Add prefetch-effectiveness metrics, token-position heatmap, kernel warmup traces, dashboard panels, and SLO-aware alert. Rollout behind feature flag. See runtime/docs/prefetch-metrics.md for details.
